::: {.margin-note}
**Fall 2026 · Innopolis University** · Thursdays, Aug 27 – Dec 3 · one 90-minute lecture +
one lab per week · 3rd-year BS, Data Science track
:::

Relational structure is the dominant untapped signal in industrial data. A working ML
engineer meets it as the knowledge graph grounding an LLM system, as a recommender's
user–item graph, as a fraud ring in a transaction network, as a molecule — and, most often,
as the relational database their company already owns. This course teaches you to
**represent** such data (graphs, heterogeneous graphs, knowledge graphs), to **learn** from
it (shallow embeddings → graph neural networks → graph transformers), and to **reason**
over it (KG embeddings, multi-hop queries, GraphRAG).

By the end of the course a strong student can read a current NeurIPS/ICLR graph-ML paper
and implement it; every student can use PyTorch Geometric on a real problem and defend each
design choice.

## Start here

The course begins **Thursday, August 27, 2026** with
[Week 1: Why graphs?](lectures/01-why-graphs.qmd) and its
[onboarding lab](labs/lab01.qmd) — set up your environment there first, then continue
into [Week 2: classical graph ML](lectures/02-classical-graph-ml.qmd), where structure
starts answering questions. Materials go live week by week; the
[GCN week](lectures/06-gcn.qmd) is also published and shows where the course is headed:
interactive lecture pages you can manipulate, and Colab labs that build each method
from scratch before reaching for the library.

## How the course works

| | |
|---|---|
| **Lectures** | Interactive articles in the spirit of [Distill](https://distill.pub/2021/gnn-intro/) — read them, play with them, print them; class is taught directly from these pages |
| **Labs** | One Colab notebook per week; runs on the free tier end-to-end; from-scratch first, then PyTorch Geometric |
| **Grading** | Labs 15% (best 12 of 14) · Homeworks 30% (3 × 10%) · Midterm 15% (Wk 8, Oct 15) · Project 20% · Final 20% (Wk 15, Dec 3) |
| **AI policy** | AI assistants are allowed for labs, homework, and the project **with mandatory disclosure**, and you must be able to explain any line you submit. Exams: no aids beyond the final's cheat sheet. |

See the full [syllabus](syllabus.qmd), the annotated [reading list](reading-list.qmd), and
the [notation reference](notation.qmd) used across all fifteen weeks.
